description: Returns submission-deadline changes for one watched TED tender, from its official TED notices: each event per lot with old and new deadline (local and UTC), plus the current deadlines. Use it after tenders_list_watched gave you a notice_id; use funding_list_changes for grant calls and compliance_list_deadlines for legal dates. Inputs: notice_id (required, TED publication number, e.g. 662865-2026), limit (1 to 50, default 50) and cursor (next_cursor to page or checkpoint_cursor to poll later; cursors belong to that notice and expire after 24 hours). Output: events[] with lot, old and new deadlines and the TED notice link, current deadlines, cursors and freshness (checked hourly). A notice we do not watch returns notice_not_tracked. Terms: read-only; MCP calls are never charged. Without a key, metered routes give 10 successful answers a day free, as short samples (up to 3 records, without file proof, history or paging cursor) where a paid HTTP address exists (unmetered routes are unlimited); errors do not count. On the paid HTTP routes, errors are free, and so are empty answers except a sanctions name search with no match when every loaded list it checks is fresh (lists not loaded yet are named in the answer). An optional API key keeps its prepaid-credit policy. When the free answers run out, the error names the HTTP alternative.

cursor.description: Opaque signed base64url next_cursor or checkpoint_cursor for this same notice, 20 to 400 ASCII letters/digits/_/-. Copy unchanged; refresh within 24 hours; omit on first call. Example illustrates syntax only, not a valid signature.

notice_id.description: TED publication number of the watched tender, e.g. 662865-2026
